title: How do we spot a wrong protractor reading?
description: A student has measured six angles with a protractor, and some readings are wrong. Three checks are written one by one on the board: the centre on the vertex, one arm on the zero line, and the scale read from that zero. Keeko doubts the first check and thinks the protractor can sit anywhere on an arm.
teaching_notes: One idea: a protractor reading is right only when the centre is on the vertex, one arm is on the zero line, and the scale is read from that zero. Watch for students who slide the protractor along an arm and trust the new number.

source: A student used a protractor to measure the angles as shown b
video_script.why: The child learns three checks for using a protractor correctly, and uses them to find the mistakes in someone else's measuring.
video_script.substitution: The six angles of the book's box Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake.
video_script.anchor: the protractor of the book, with its centre point, its zero lines and its inner and outer scales
video_script.wrong_answer: the protractor can go anywhere, as long as it touches an arm
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the protractor can go anywhere, as long as it touches an arm. Sliding the protractor along an arm changes the number but not the angle, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: A reading is right only when all three checks pass

final_answer.value: the centre on the vertex, one arm on the zero line, and the scale read from that zero

maths_rules: check 1: the centre of the protractor lies exactly on the vertex of the angle
check 2: one arm of the angle lies along the 0 line of the protractor
check 3: read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm, the inner or the outer one
the six readings in the book are angle U = 35 degrees, V = 80 degrees, W = 70 degrees, X = 150 degrees, Y = 120 degrees, Z = 85 degrees
the book prints no solution, so no single reading is judged right or wrong here
slip: sliding the protractor along an arm changes the reading but not the angle
video_script.design: One idea: three checks make a protractor reading trustworthy. The protractor stays on the board all video, and one tick lights up for each check.
open_questions: The book prints no solution for this discussion box, and the six figures are not in the extracted text, so the video teaches the three checks without judging any one figure.

narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, check that the centre of the protractor lies exactly on the vertex of the angle.
<bookmark mark='why'/>An angle is measured at its vertex. A protractor placed away from it measures some other angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: one arm of the angle must lie along the 0 line

marks.zero: one arm turns onto the zero line and a second tick lights up
marks.why: the count 0, 10, 20 runs out from the zero line

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns until the zero line meets one arm
narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step two, check that one arm of the angle lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The count of degrees starts at zero. The arm we start from must sit exactly there.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm, inner or outer

narration: <bookmark mark='scale'/>Step three, read the scale that starts at zero on that arm. It may be the inner one or the outer one.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The other scale counts from the other end, so it gives a different number.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a reading is right only when all three checks pass; if one fails, place the protractor again

marks.fix: an arrow points back to the failed check to place the protractor again

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A reading is right only when all three checks pass.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>If one check fails, place the protractor again and read the new number.
